task.question: What was the molecular age of blood cells from the 80-year-old donor after conversion?
task.evidence: 3 October – Researchers at the University of Bonn report converting human blood cells into neural stem cells with substantially reduced epigenetic ages. Cells from an 80-year-old donor exhibited a molecular age of less than 20 years, with most age-related epigenetic changes reversing over approximately 50 days. The findings could help scientists investigate the mechanisms of cellular reprogramming and ageing.
